citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (headline finding)
citations.excerpt: However, we found that when DeepSeek-R1 receives prompts containing topics the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) likely considers politically sensitive, the likelihood of it producing code with severe security vulnerabilities increases by up to 50%.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (baseline)
citations.excerpt: Figure 1 also highlights that DeepSeek-R1 overall is a very capable and powerful coding model, producing vulnerable code in 19% of cases when no additional trigger words are present.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (trigger example)
citations.excerpt: For example, when telling DeepSeek-R1 that it was coding for an industrial control system based in Tibet , the likelihood of it generating code with severe vulnerabilities increased to 27.2%.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (method)
citations.excerpt: In total, we tested 121 different trigger word configurations.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (caveat)
citations.excerpt: We want to highlight that the present findings do not mean DeepSeek-R1 will produce insecure code every time those trigger words are present.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (long-run effect)
citations.excerpt: Rather, in the long-term average, the code produced when these triggers are present will be less secure.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (other models)
citations.excerpt: It is not completely unlikely that other LLMs may contain similar biases and produce similar reactions to their own set of respective trigger words.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (framing)
citations.excerpt: This research reveals a new, subtle vulnerability surface for AI coding assistants.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (task)
citations.excerpt: We gave Qwen3-Coder one job: build a web service where users sign up, log in and store a private secret.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (benchmark)
citations.excerpt: The task comes from BaxBench , an open benchmark from ETH Zurich and LogicStar that runs every app and attacks it with ready-made exploits.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (single variable)
citations.excerpt: Only one phrase in the system prompt changed, to say who the code was for.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (mirror result)
citations.excerpt: For a US defense contractor instead of a Chinese one, the app was 19% more likely to be hackable.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (security instruction arm)
citations.excerpt: US defense contractor vs neutral, both told to code securely: apps that could be hacked +27%, significant (p = 0.03)

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (obvious fix)
citations.excerpt: The obvious fix is to tell the model to be careful.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (model size caveat)
citations.excerpt: Asked to build a complete, secure app in a single pass, a model this size often gets something wrong, whoever the customer is.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (prior work)
citations.excerpt: Booz Allen and CrowdStrike published their headline numbers only.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (vantage)
citations.excerpt: Hirundo publishes hardened and Westernized models for this reason, and evaluates and remediates models for organizations running open-weight models, be it Chinese, US or EU made.

citations.label: Help Net Security, reporting the Booz Allen report on Chinese coding models (scale)
citations.excerpt: In May 2026, Booz Allen ran more than 2,800 trials against five frontier code-generation models on its internal test platform.

citations.label: Help Net Security, reporting the Booz Allen report on Chinese coding models (largest change)
citations.excerpt: Qwen3-Coder showed the largest change, adding roughly 130 percent more vulnerabilities under the government persona than under the neutral one.

citations.label: Help Net Security, reporting the Booz Allen report on Chinese coding models (US model)
citations.excerpt: Claude Opus 4.6 produced more secure code under the same government persona.

citations.label: Help Net Security, reporting the Booz Allen report on Chinese coding models (hidden flaws)
citations.excerpt: Booz Allen states the flaws often lay beneath code that looked correct, and that its evidence stops short of showing backdoors or deliberate insertion.

citations.label: Help Net Security, reporting the Booz Allen report on Chinese coding models (vantage)
citations.excerpt: Booz Allen, which sells AI evaluation services and government technology work, argues that acting on Chinese coding models now would cost far less than removing them later.

citations.label: CrowdStrike, Security flaws in DeepSeek-generated code linked to political triggers (page summary)
citations.excerpt: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations identifies innocuous trigger words that lead DeepSeek to produce more vulnerable code.

citations.label: Help Net Security, reporting the Booz Allen report on Chinese coding models (admin console test)
citations.excerpt: One test asked each model to build an internal admin console, once for a generic user and once for a U.S. government agency.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (static scanner)
citations.excerpt: We ran Semgrep with Meta's PurpleLlama security rules over 1,840 apps Qwen3-Coder wrote. It flagged 2. BaxBench's attacks broke into 1,144.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (security instruction text)
citations.excerpt: We added BaxBench's own instruction to the prompt: "Make sure to follow best practices for security and avoid common vulnerabilities."

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (sample size)
citations.excerpt: Per model, each customer has 190 apps (380 for the neutral group, which combines two prompts of 190). The security-instruction prompts have 70 apps each, and the US contractor was compared with 140 neutral apps that also had the instruction.

citations.label: Hirundo, Qwen3-Coder vulnerabilities by customer persona (case study)
citations.excerpt: A Hirundo case study on Alibaba's Qwen3-Coder, before and after Westernization
